name: Heart Leaf Philodendron
currentStatus: Sharing a pot with the snake plant — watch the water balance
headline: The plain green form of the same species as your Brasil — and the more forgiving of the two.
water: Top 1–2" dry, then water thoroughly (~10 days). NOTE: it shares a pot with a snake plant, which wants to dry out far harder. Water to the SNAKE PLANT's schedule and mist/spot-water this one, or the shared root zone stays wet and the snake plant rots.
light: Medium to bright indirect. Tolerates lower light better than almost anything else you own, but gets leggy with big gaps between leaves if it is too dim.
soil: Aroid mix — potting soil + perlite + bark. In a shared pot, err chunkier for the snake plant's sake.
fertilizer: Balanced, monthly spring–summer. Feed on the lighter side in a shared pot.
repot: Every 1–2 yrs — and this is the moment to separate the two if you want them on their own schedules.
propagate: Very easy. Cut below a node, root in water or straight into soil.
tips: Same species as your Brasil, just without the variegation — care is identical.
Pinch the vines back to keep it full instead of stringy.
The aerial nubs along the stem are where roots form; bury one to encourage rooting.
Sap is a mild irritant — wash hands after pruning.

issues.fix: Too little light; move brighter and pinch back.
Overwatering — very likely in a pot shared with a snake plant.
Dry air or letting it go bone dry too long.
